nominations.contribution: for developing quantitative general-equilibrium models of trade based on comparative advantage and geography
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: Eaton-Kortum turned Ricardian theory into a tractable, estimable general-equilibrium workhorse that underpins nearly all modern counterfactual trade-policy analysis. It is exactly the kind of mapping from closed-form theory to quantitative policy conclusions I value. The reservation is that the welfare conclusions are sensitive to the trade elasticity.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of innovation, imperfect competition and the political economy of trade
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
Helpman and Krugman, 1985: Market Structure and Foreign Trade, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: Their joint work links trade, endogenous technical change and the politics of protection in coherent dynamic frameworks with broad cross-field influence. The core contribution spans several areas, which is both a strength and an attribution challenge. Part of the monopolistic-competition work overlaps with Krugman's 2008 prize.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm heterogeneity in international trade
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
Bernard and Jensen, 1999: Exceptional Exporter Performance: Cause, Effect, or Both?, Journal of International Economics
nominations.rationale: Bernard and Jensen documented exporter heterogeneity and Melitz provided the tractable model, which is now the field's standard. The reallocation channel changed how gains from trade are understood. The candidates are relatively young, so the timing may be early.

nominations.contribution: for the development of the micro-founded new open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: They brought dynamic general equilibrium with nominal rigidities into open-economy macro, replacing the Mundell-Fleming framework as the analytical standard. It is a clear methodological transformation. The empirical success on exchange rates remains limited.

nominations.contribution: for the theoretical foundation of the gravity equation of international trade
key_works: Anderson, 1979: A Theoretical Foundation for the Gravity Equation, American Economic Review
Anderson and van Wincoop, 2003: Gravity with Gravitas, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They provided the theory behind the most robust empirical regularity in trade and corrected its estimation through multilateral resistance. The result is widely used in policy evaluation. It may be judged narrower than the frameworks ranked above.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm heterogeneity in international trade and investment
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The impact of trade on intra-industry reallocations and aggregate industry productivity, Econometrica
Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple, 2004: Export versus FDI with heterogeneous firms, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This is a clean and general model that reorganized trade theory and empirics. It is distinct from Krugman's prize, though it builds on it.

nominations.contribution: for founding the new open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange rate dynamics redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: They built microfounded, welfare-based open-economy policy analysis. The framework is foundational and widely used.

nominations.contribution: for developing the Ricardian probabilistic model underlying quantitative general-equilibrium trade analysis
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, geography, and trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: An elegant, tractable structure made counterfactual trade policy evaluation operational. That is a real bridge from theory to practice.

nominations.contribution: for the political-economy analysis of trade policy
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for sale, American Economic Review
Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: This is a clean game-theoretic model of how policy is determined. Its empirical support is mixed.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of capital-flow reversals and crises in emerging economies
key_works: Calvo, 1998: Capital flows and capital-market crises: the simple economics of sudden stops, Journal of Applied Economics
nominations.rationale: The work has been highly influential for policy, and Calvo pricing is a further contribution. It is less of a unified theoretical frontier.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of the interaction between trade, innovation and the political economy of trade policy
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for sale, American Economic Review
Helpman and Krugman, 1985: Market Structure and Foreign Trade, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: This is a broad, cumulative theoretical program that has shaped trade theory for three decades. The protection-for-sale model has been taken to data repeatedly. Its structural estimates imply implausibly high weights on welfare, which is a reservation about its empirical fit.

nominations.contribution: for the development of quantitative models of trade with heterogeneous firms and technologies
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, geography, and trade, Econometrica
Melitz, 2003: The impact of trade on intra-industry reallocations and aggregate industry productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: These models rest on a robust stylized fact, exporter premia, that has been documented in firm data across dozens of countries. They gave the field a common quantitative toolkit. The welfare conclusions depend heavily on a few elasticities, so the choice of those parameters drives much of the result.

nominations.contribution: for the foundations of modern open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange rate dynamics redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: Their framework provided the microfounded basis for exchange-rate and policy analysis in open economies. They have also documented puzzles candidly, which is a valuable scientific habit. Exchange-rate prediction nonetheless remains poor, a point Rogoff's own work with Meese established.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of the local labor-market effects of import competition
key_works: Autor, Dorn and Hanson, 2013: The China syndrome: local labor market effects of import competition in the United States, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: The China-shock findings have been reproduced in several other countries and have reshaped both research and policy debate. Recent methodological work on shift-share designs has examined the instrument closely. The core result has largely survived that scrutiny, though some magnitudes are debated.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of the global financial cycle and dominant-currency pricing
key_works: Rey, 2013: Dilemma not trilemma: the global financial cycle and monetary policy independence, Jackson Hole Symposium
Gopinath, Boz, Casas, Díez, Gourinchas and Plagborg-Møller, 2020: Dominant currency paradigm, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Both strands challenge textbook Mundell-Fleming conclusions with large datasets. The findings are influential and growing. They are less mature, and I would want more independent confirmation before ranking them higher.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of innovation, growth and the political economy of trade policy in the global economy
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This is a deep, coherent theoretical program spanning dynamic trade, endogenous protection and offshoring. It is complementary to Krugman's 2008 prize rather than a duplicate of it.

nominations.contribution: for the development of quantitative Ricardian models of international trade
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: Their model made counterfactual welfare analysis of trade policy a standard empirical tool. Its general-equilibrium structure is a strength. The results rest heavily on functional-form assumptions.

nominations.contribution: for the development of the micro-founded intertemporal approach to open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: They set the modern framework for exchange-rate and current-account analysis. The empirical performance of exchange-rate models remains weak.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm heterogeneity in international trade
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: This work brought micro-data evidence on exporters into trade theory and reshaped the field. Melitz is relatively young, so the prize may come later.

nominations.contribution: for credible empirical analysis of the labor-market consequences of import competition
key_works: Autor, Dorn and Hanson, 2013: The China Syndrome, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Long-run, local-labor-market evidence of this kind is exactly what short-run aggregate studies miss, and it changed the policy debate. The shift-share identification and the neglect of general-equilibrium offsets are my reservations.

nominations.contribution: for integrating imperfect competition, innovation and political economy into the theory of international trade
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
Helpman and Krugman, 1985: Market Structure and Foreign Trade, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: This is a broad, durable agenda that combines theory with testable political-economy mechanisms. 'Protection for Sale' in particular has been confronted with data repeatedly. The main reservation is proximity to Krugman's 2008 prize.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm heterogeneity and the quantitative theory of trade flows
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: This work links firm-level micro data to aggregate productivity through reallocation, a precise mechanism of real effects. It underpins modern quantitative trade policy evaluation. Melitz is young relative to past laureates.

nominations.contribution: for the foundations of new open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: This work built microfounded open-economy models that now dominate international macro policy analysis. Its influence is broad. Exchange-rate puzzles remain only partly resolved.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of incomplete contracts and the organization of global production
key_works: Antràs, 2003: Firms, Contracts, and Trade Structure, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Antràs and Helpman, 2004: Global Sourcing, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Antràs brings property-rights theory of the firm to bear on global value chains and tests it against intrafirm trade data, exactly the theory-to-data link I value. He is still very young for the prize.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of capital flows, sudden stops and emerging-market crises
key_works: Calvo, 1998: Capital Flows and Capital-Market Crises: The Simple Economics of Sudden Stops, Journal of Applied Economics
Calvo, 1983: Staggered Prices in a Utility-Maximizing Framework, Journal of Monetary Economics
nominations.rationale: Calvo identified the financial-flow mechanism behind emerging-market crises, which has shaped IMF practice. His pricing model is also ubiquitous. The contribution is split across fields.

nominations.contribution: for integrating innovation, endogenous growth and political economy into the theory of international trade
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This is a tractable dynamic general-equilibrium framework that links openness to long-run growth. It has been widely built upon. The reservation is its partial overlap with the 2008 and 2018 prizes.

nominations.contribution: for quantitative trade theory based on firm heterogeneity and Ricardian technology
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: These models made trade theory quantitative and disciplined by micro data. They are standard tools for counterfactual analysis. The age spread among the three is large.

nominations.contribution: for microfounded open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: They replaced ad hoc open-economy models with an intertemporal general-equilibrium framework. The reservation is that exchange-rate puzzles remain largely unresolved.

nominations.contribution: for the duality-based general-equilibrium theory of international trade
key_works: Dixit and Norman, 1980: Theory of International Trade, Cambridge University Press
Dixit and Stiglitz, 1977: Monopolistic Competition and Optimum Product Diversity, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Dixit-Stiglitz preferences underpin modern trade, growth and macroeconomics. The work's breadth is a strength, but its trade-specific core is older and in part already recognized through Krugman.

nominations.contribution: for measuring the gains from new varieties and constructing trade-consistent price indexes
key_works: Feenstra, 1994: New Product Varieties and the Measurement of International Prices, American Economic Review
Broda and Weinstein, 2006: Globalization and the Gains from Variety, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: This work corrects price indexes for new goods, a measurement issue central to growth and inflation accounting. Its scope is narrower than the frameworks ranked above.

nominations.contribution: for developing the quantitative Ricardian theory of trade and geography
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
Eaton and Kortum, 1999: International Technology Diffusion: Theory and Measurement, International Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Their framework underpins modern quantitative trade and spatial economics. It is widely applied to historical market integration and to railway rollouts, as in Donaldson's work. It is a genuine tool that the field builds on.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of innovation, growth and the political economy of trade policy in the global economy
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Their work integrated trade with endogenous technology and with political economy. It has been foundational for decades. The reservation is partial proximity to Krugman's 2008 award.

nominations.contribution: for the historical analysis of globalization, factor-price convergence and mass migration
key_works: O'Rourke and Williamson, 1999: Globalization and History, MIT Press
Hatton and Williamson, 1998: The Age of Mass Migration, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: Their newly constructed price and wage series tested Heckscher-Ohlin predictions over a century and across the Atlantic economy, including Scandinavia. This is exactly the long-horizon validation I value. The reservation is Williamson's advanced age and the work's more descriptive identification.

nominations.contribution: for founding the new open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: They provided microfounded open-economy macro and a dominant textbook framework. They are also historically literate on exchange-rate regimes. Its impact is somewhat narrower than the trade nominations above.

nominations.contribution: for the theory of international trade with heterogeneous firms
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: This is the most cited trade theory paper of its generation and is matched to firm-level data. The reservation is youth; the award would better come later.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm heterogeneity in international trade
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
Bernard and Jensen, 1999: Exceptional Exporter Performance: Cause, Effect, or Both?, Journal of International Economics
Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, 2003: Plants and Productivity in International Trade, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Here micro facts about exporting plants led to a new theory that durably changed the entire field. This is the firm-level lens I favour. Credit is well defined: the empirical discovery came from Bernard and Jensen, the canonical model from Melitz.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of trade policy, trade and growth, and the organization of global production
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Helpman and Krugman, 1985: Market Structure and Foreign Trade, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: This is a broad and deep body of work on imperfect competition, political economy and trade. My reservation is the overlap with Krugman's 2008 prize and the breadth of the work, which makes a sharp motivation harder to write.

nominations.contribution: for developing the quantitative Ricardian theory of trade
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
Eaton, Kortum and Kramarz, 2011: An Anatomy of International Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: This work created the workhorse for counterfactual trade policy evaluation. My reservation is that its aggregate structure rests on strong distributional assumptions that micro data only partly discipline.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of exchange-rate pass-through, pricing-to-market and the role of invoicing currencies
key_works: Goldberg and Knetter, 1997: Goods Prices and Exchange Rates: What Have We Learned?, Journal of Economic Literature
Gopinath, Itskhoki and Rigobon, 2010: Currency Choice and Exchange Rate Pass-Through, American Economic Review
Engel, 1999: Accounting for U.S. Real Exchange Rate Changes, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: This is close to my own research and links firm pricing and invoicing choices to macro outcomes using transaction-level data. My reservations are that the dominant-currency paradigm is recent and that I must guard against my own bias toward this area.

nominations.contribution: for founding the new open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
Meese and Rogoff, 1983: Empirical Exchange Rate Models of the Seventies, Journal of International Economics
nominations.rationale: This work brought optimizing price-setting firms into open-economy macroeconomics, and it changed models for decades. My reservation is that its producer-currency pricing assumptions were later contradicted by the micro evidence on invoicing.

nominations.contribution: for developing quantitative trade theory with heterogeneous firms and technologies
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: Together these models restructured the field and tied trade theory closely to firm-level micro data. The core of the contribution is clearly distinct from Krugman's 2008 prize, although it builds on it.

nominations.contribution: for credible measurement of the labor-market consequences of import competition
key_works: Autor, Dorn and Hanson, 2013: The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Their shift-share design changed both economic and political understanding of trade's distributional costs, and later work linked the shock to crime and family outcomes. My reservation is that shift-share identification is still debated, and the contribution may be early for a prize.

nominations.contribution: for the foundations of new open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: They created the standard microfounded framework for open-economy policy analysis. The empirical predictive record on exchange rates remains weak.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of trade, innovation and the political economy of trade policy
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Protection for Sale models trade policy as an institutional outcome shaped by lobbying, a lens I value. The work is broad and influential, but its empirical tests have mixed identification.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of capital flows and sudden stops in emerging economies
key_works: Calvo, 1998: Capital Flows and Capital-Market Crises: The Simple Economics of Sudden Stops, Journal of Applied Economics
Calvo, 1983: Staggered Prices in a Utility-Maximizing Framework, Journal of Monetary Economics
nominations.rationale: Calvo has made two lasting contributions: sudden stops and Calvo pricing. The case is policy-relevant, but his credit for sudden stops is shared with a broad literature.

nominations.contribution: for integrating innovation, growth and the political economy of trade policy into international trade theory
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
Grossman and Helpman, 2001: Special Interest Politics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: Protection for Sale gave a testable model of how organized interests shape trade policy, and it is widely used in political science. Together with their work on trade and growth, this is a broad and mature body of work. Empirical tests of the lobbying model rely on weak proxies for political organization.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm heterogeneity in international trade
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
Bernard and Jensen, 1999: Exceptional Exporter Performance: Cause, Effect, or Both?, Journal of International Economics
nominations.rationale: Microdata on exporters combined with the Melitz model changed how trade is studied, which is a case of new data reshaping the field. Melitz is young relative to laureate norms.

nominations.contribution: for the foundations of modern open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: They built the standard framework for exchange rates and international policy. Rogoff's long-run historical data work on crises and debt also fits a comparative-historical perspective.

nominations.contribution: for quantitative Ricardian models of trade and geography
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: This tractable framework enabled cumulative quantitative work and counterfactual policy analysis. It is methodologically central, though less connected to institutions.

nominations.contribution: for the historical analysis of the international monetary system
key_works: Eichengreen, 1992: Golden Fetters: The Gold Standard and the Great Depression, 1919-1939, Oxford University Press
Eichengreen and Sachs, 1985: Exchange Rates and Economic Recovery in the 1930s, Journal of Economic History
nominations.rationale: Long-run comparative evidence on how monetary regimes interact with domestic politics, including the extension of the franchise, is exactly the kind of work that travels across periods and countries. It may be read as economic history rather than trade.

nominations.contribution: for developing quantitative general-equilibrium models of international trade with Ricardian technology and geography
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
Arkolakis, Costinot and Rodríguez-Clare, 2012: New Trade Models, Same Old Gains?, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Eaton–Kortum turned trade theory into a tractable, estimable general-equilibrium framework that now underlies counterfactual analysis of trade policy, gains from trade and spatial economics. The sufficient-statistic result for the gains from trade is a model of analytical tractability linked to credible magnitudes. One open question is whether to include Costinot or Arkolakis rather than Rodríguez-Clare.

nominations.contribution: for the theory of trade with heterogeneous firms
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple, 2004: Export versus FDI with Heterogeneous Firms, American Economic Review
Helpman and Krugman, 1985: Market Structure and Foreign Trade, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: The Melitz model is the dominant workhorse of modern trade: it explains reallocation across firms as a general-equilibrium productivity mechanism. Helpman's broad contributions to imperfect-competition trade theory complement it. My reservation is that it sits close to Krugman's 2008 prize and that the aggregate gains may not exceed those of simpler models.

nominations.contribution: for the development of the new open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: They gave international macroeconomics dynamic, optimizing general-equilibrium foundations with nominal rigidities, enabling welfare analysis of exchange-rate regimes. The framework became the standard in open-economy policy analysis. Its exchange-rate predictions remain empirically weak.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of the political economy of trade policy and of trade and innovation
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Grossman and Rossi-Hansberg, 2008: Trading Tasks: A Simple Theory of Offshoring, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: The work offers equilibrium mechanisms linking interest groups, innovation and offshoring to trade outcomes, and these have been widely used. Helpman is a co-author of much of it but is listed with the heterogeneous-firms nomination. The breadth of the contribution makes it hard to pin down a single core.

nominations.contribution: for the discovery of the global financial cycle and its implications for monetary autonomy
key_works: Rey, 2013: Dilemma not Trilemma: The Global Financial Cycle and Monetary Policy Independence, Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium
Gourinchas and Rey, 2007: International Financial Adjustment, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: The work reshaped thinking on capital flows and the Mundellian trilemma. Its mechanism is still mostly empirical and is only partially embedded in a structural equilibrium model. The candidate is also young.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm heterogeneity and reallocation in international trade
key_works: Melitz, 2003: "The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity", Econometrica
Melitz and Ottaviano, 2008: "Market Size, Trade, and Productivity", Review of Economic Studies
Melitz and Redding, 2014: "Heterogeneous Firms and Trade", in Handbook of International Economics
nominations.rationale: The Melitz model changed trade theory by making selection, productivity dispersion and within-industry reallocation central to the gains from trade. It is simple enough to be a workhorse and rich enough to discipline empirical and quantitative work. The reservation is that the candidate is younger than the typical laureate, though the contribution is already mature.

nominations.contribution: for the development of quantitative Ricardian models of international trade and technology-driven specialization
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: "Technology, Geography, and Trade", Econometrica
Eaton and Kortum, 2012: "Putting Ricardo to Work", Journal of Economic Perspectives
Eaton, Kortum and Kramarz, 2011: "An Anatomy of International Trade: Evidence from French Firms", Econometrica
nominations.rationale: Eaton and Kortum gave the Ricardian model a tractable stochastic structure that can be taken to data and used for counterfactual welfare analysis. This is precisely the kind of mechanism-based quantitative framework that reshaped a field. The reservation is that its empirical implementation relies on strong structure and on parameters whose interpretation can vary across applications.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of incomplete contracts and the organization of global production
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 2002: "Integration versus Outsourcing in Industry Equilibrium", Quarterly Journal of Economics
Antràs, 2003: "Firms, Contracts, and Trade Structure", Quarterly Journal of Economics
Antràs and Helpman, 2004: "Global Sourcing", Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: This line made the boundaries of firms and global value chains endogenous to contracting frictions, ownership and location. It is a clear mechanism that links trade, organization and welfare in general equilibrium. The reservation is that part of the underlying property-rights theory belongs to a separately recognized contract-theory literature.

nominations.contribution: for the intertemporal approach to open-economy macroeconomics and exchange-rate dynamics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: "Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux", Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 2000: "The Six Major Puzzles in International Macroeconomics: Is There a Common Cause?", NBER Macroeconomics Annual
nominations.rationale: Their work made intertemporal optimization and general equilibrium the organizing language of international macroeconomics. It provided durable benchmarks for current accounts, exchange rates and policy in open economies. The reservation is that some of the empirical exchange-rate puzzles remain unresolved by the framework itself.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of globalization, offshoring and labor-market adjustment
key_works: Feenstra and Hanson, 1996: "Globalization, Outsourcing, and Wage Inequality", American Economic Review
Feenstra and Hanson, 1999: "The Impact of Outsourcing and High-Technology Capital on Wages", Quarterly Journal of Economics
Autor, Dorn and Hanson, 2013: "The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States", American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This work changed how economists measure the distributional effects of trade and offshoring, moving the field beyond representative-agent gains. It is policy-relevant because it identifies adjustment costs and local labor-market persistence. The reservation is that attribution is more diffuse and part of the contribution borders labor economics.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm heterogeneity in international trade

people.name: Elhanan Helpman
people.affiliation: Harvard University and Tel Aviv University

key_works: Bernard and Jensen, 1995: Exporters, Jobs, and Wages in U.S. Manufacturing: 1976-1987, Brookings Papers on Economic Activity: Microeconomics
Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple, 2004: Export versus FDI with Heterogeneous Firms, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This contribution changed the unit of analysis in trade from industries to firms and gave a sharp selection mechanism for export participation and productivity gains. It combines elegant theory with large measured welfare and reallocation effects. The reservation is that it is a younger contribution than some classic trade candidates, though its influence is already pervasive.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of global production, offshoring and trade in tasks
key_works: Antràs, 2003: Firms, Contracts, and Trade Structure, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Grossman and Rossi-Hansberg, 2008: Trading Tasks: A Simple Theory of Offshoring, American Economic Review
Antràs and Helpman, 2004: Global Sourcing, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: The work supplies the conceptual tools for thinking about production networks rather than only trade in final goods. Its mechanism—contracting and task allocation across borders—travels well across modern global value chains. The reservation is that the empirical implementation is dispersed across a broad subsequent literature.

nominations.contribution: for the structural gravity theory of international trade
key_works: Anderson, 1979: A theoretical foundation for the gravity equation, American Economic Review
Anderson and van Wincoop, 2003: Gravity with gravitas: A solution to the border puzzle, American Economic Review
Anderson and van Wincoop, 2004: Trade costs, Journal of Economic Literature
nominations.rationale: Structural gravity converted a successful empirical regularity into an equilibrium system suitable for welfare analysis and counterfactuals. The multilateral-resistance insight is now standard in both academic and policy work. The reservation is that gravity is a method and accounting structure as much as a full theory of trade mechanisms.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of global production, offshoring and task trade
key_works: Grossman and Rossi-Hansberg, 2008: Trading tasks: A simple theory of offshoring, American Economic Review
Antràs and Helpman, 2004: Global sourcing, Journal of Political Economy
Antràs, 2003: Firms, contracts, and trade structure, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: This work explains modern trade as trade in tasks and organization of production, not merely final goods. It gives coherent mechanisms for wage effects, firm boundaries and the geography of value chains. The reservation is that the field is still young relative to older trade contributions.

nominations.contribution: for the intertemporal and microfounded analysis of open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange rate dynamics redux, Journal of Political Economy
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1996: Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press
Obstfeld and Rogoff, 2000: The six major puzzles in international macroeconomics: Is there a common cause?, NBER Macroeconomics Annual
nominations.rationale: Their work supplied the main dynamic general-equilibrium language for exchange rates, current accounts and international policy interdependence. It has shaped both teaching and research in open-economy macro. The reservation is that international macro has struggled to produce quantitatively successful exchange-rate models.

nominations.contribution: for their quantitative general equilibrium models of international trade and the diffusion of technologies
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: They introduced a tractable, probabilistically grounded formulation of comparative advantage that seamlessly maps into multi-country general equilibrium. This rigorous methodological advance transformed trade from qualitative theory into a highly quantitative policy science. It provides a durable foundation for evaluating global trade frictions and welfare tradeoffs.

nominations.contribution: for his firm-level framework for analyzing international trade and macroeconomic dynamics
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: By introducing heterogeneous firm productivity into dynamic general equilibrium, Melitz created the definitive modern framework for trade analysis. It elegantly captures how intra-industry reallocation affects long-run productivity and welfare. The result is simple, extremely general, and a foundational building block for subsequent quantitative trade theory.

nominations.contribution: for their analysis of the political economy of trade policy and dynamic frameworks of trade and growth
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They successfully integrated endogenous technological change and political-economy incentives into rigorous models of international trade. Their work clarifies exactly how special interests distort optimal policy and how trade interacts with long-run growth. It stands as a prime example of mapping clear micro-incentives into broad macroeconomic consequences.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the theory of global value chains and the organizational boundaries of multinational firms
key_works: Antras, 2003: Firms, Contracts, and Trade Structure, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: Antras brought the theory of incomplete contracts into international trade, providing a structural explanation for the boundaries of the multinational firm. His framework rigorously maps institutional frictions into the general equilibrium of global value chains. The work is crucial for understanding the real-world complexities of modern industrial production.

nominations.contribution: for his empirical analysis of the macroeconomic and labor market consequences of international trade shocks
key_works: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson, 2013: The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Autor meticulously documented the long-lasting employment and political consequences of trade exposure in local labor markets. While deeply empirical, the findings have profound implications for evaluating the welfare and distributional costs of trade in general equilibrium. His evidence highlights the slow adjustment dynamics that standard theory often obscures.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of international trade with heterogeneous firms
key_works: Melitz, M. J., 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: He provided a mathematically elegant, highly tractable model that sharply characterizes the selection mechanisms of heterogeneous firms in international markets. I appreciate the clean theoretical frontiers that have organized a vast body of applied work and quantified welfare gains.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of the political economy of trade policy
key_works: Grossman, G. M., & Helpman, E., 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Their framework brilliantly applies common-agency game theory to map out the institutional and strategic constraints of trade policy. It is a foundational possibility result for understanding how special interests distort optimal allocations.

nominations.contribution: for the development of quantitative models of international trade
key_works: Eaton, J., & Kortum, S., 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: They transformed abstract Ricardian theory into a quantifiable mechanism, allowing the robust measurement of trade welfare gains. The rigorous mapping from axiomatic theory to empirical structural models is exemplary.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of global value chains and the boundaries of the multinational firm
key_works: Antràs, P., 2003: Firms, Contracts, and Trade Structure, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: His integration of incomplete contracts into global value chains formally shows how firm boundaries are endogenously determined. This axiomatic-style organizational modeling is formally precise and practically relevant for understanding global allocations.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the spatial distribution of economic activity and the economics of globalization
nominations.rationale: His models of economic geography yield clear, structural insights into the spatial allocation of production. The results are conceptually clean and continue to guide both regional institutional design and global trade policy.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of the labor market consequences of international trade
key_works: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson, 2013: The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This contribution shifted international trade towards highly credible, well-powered empirical designs by utilizing massive administrative datasets to identify the local economic impacts of global trade shocks. The findings on the 'China Shock' have been heavily replicated and shown remarkable robustness across different analytical choices and contexts. This is a model for establishing cumulative, reliable knowledge in an applied field.

nominations.contribution: for the theory of firm heterogeneity and its implications for international trade
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: While a theoretical breakthrough, this model explicitly incorporated firm-level differences, which immediately enabled researchers to test trade theories using massive, highly powered firm-level customs datasets. It successfully transformed trade from studying aggregates to analyzing granular micro-data. I strongly value theory that yields testable, falsifiable predictions that hold up across independent empirical investigations.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of dominant currency pricing and its implications for international macroeconomics
key_works: Gopinath, Boz, Casas, Diez, Gourinchas, and Plagborg-Moller, 2020: Dominant Currency Paradigm, American Economic Review
Gopinath and Rigobon, 2008: Sticky Borders, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: This research utilizes extraordinarily large micro-datasets of cross-country import and export prices to establish facts about currency invoicing that upended standard macro-trade theories. It perfectly exemplifies the value of transparent, large-scale data collection to overturn entrenched but empirically fragile assumptions. It provides highly reliable, cumulatively robust evidence for international macroeconomics.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of the political economy of trade policy
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They provided a foundational framework linking special interest lobbying to trade protection, moving trade theory into the realm of political realism. The model has generated extensive empirical testing, although one might ask whether the observational data often used to test it is sufficiently powered to cleanly isolate the mechanism. It remains a transformative, field-defining contribution.

nominations.contribution: for empirical research on trade policy, economic integration, and poverty
key_works: Goldberg and Pavcnik, 2007: Distributional Effects of Globalization in Developing Countries, Journal of Economic Literature
Pavcnik, 2002: Trade Liberalization, Exit, and Productivity Improvements: Evidence from Chilean Plants, Review of Economic Studies
nominations.rationale: This work relies on highly powered micro-data to credibly trace the impacts of trade liberalization on poverty, inequality, and firm productivity in developing economies. It grounds open-economy models in robust empirical realities rather than stylized assumptions. The reliance on rigorous identification across multiple developing-country contexts strongly supports its replicability and credibility.

nominations.contribution: for their analysis of the effects of international trade on local labor markets
key_works: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson, 2013: The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They masterfully combined quasi-experimental identification with granular data to document the long-run, spatially uneven labor market displacement caused by trade shocks. This changed how economists evaluate the distributional welfare impacts of globalization, highlighting friction in labor market adjustment.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of firm heterogeneity in international trade
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: By incorporating firm-level heterogeneity and selection into trade models, this work revolutionized the theoretical and empirical mapping of intra-industry trade. It provided the necessary structural framework for evaluating how reallocation affects aggregate productivity.

nominations.contribution: for their analysis of the political economy of trade policy and economic growth
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They provided a highly influential, structurally estimable model of how interest groups shape trade policy. The framework allows for the positive analysis of institutional design and its effects on economic outcomes.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of global value chains and the boundaries of the firm in international trade
key_works: Antras, 2003: Firms, Contracts, and Trade Structure, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: This research integrates contract theory with international trade, shifting focus toward firm-level boundaries and global supply chains. It facilitates a deeper understanding of how institutional frictions affect global matching and production.

nominations.contribution: for his quantitative analysis of spatial economics and international trade
key_works: Redding and Sturm, 2008: The Costs of Remoteness: Evidence from German Division and Reunification, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: By exploiting historical natural experiments and precise administrative data, this work isolates the causal effects of market access on spatial development. It seamlessly bridges rigorous empirical design with quantitative structural frameworks.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of global value chains and the boundaries of the multinational firm
key_works: Antràs, 2003: Firms, Contracts, and Trade Structure, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: Strömberg would deeply appreciate how this work brings the Aghion-Bolton-Hart incomplete contracting framework into international trade. It brilliantly identifies who holds control rights across borders and how these incentives determine real industry structure.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of international trade with heterogeneous firms
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: This model opens the black box of the industry, showing how trade reallocates resources among heterogeneous firms. It matches Strömberg's focus on micro-level firm dynamics and real productivity effects over aggregate financial returns.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of the labor market effects of international trade
key_works: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson, 2013: The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Autor employs outstanding empirical identification using granular regional and firm data to test trade theories. He cleanly isolates real employment outcomes rather than settling for high-level correlations.

nominations.contribution: for their quantitative models of international trade and technology diffusion
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: Their work bridges formal structural modeling with extensive real-world micro data, creating a durable framework for empirically estimating trade frictions.

nominations.contribution: for their contributions to the political economy of trade policy
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They apply institutional and incentive design frameworks to trade policy, mapping agency conflicts onto the generation of tariffs and protectionist outcomes.

nominations.contribution: for their quantitative models of international trade and the diffusion of technology
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, geography, and trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: They developed a tractable, quantitative framework for international trade that seamlessly handles multiple countries and technology diffusion. By embedding firm-level technology draws in a disciplined structural model that can be calibrated to aggregate facts, they revolutionized general-equilibrium counterfactuals. A main reservation is the strong distributional assumptions required for tractability.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of firm-level heterogeneity and its implications for international trade
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The impact of trade on intra-industry reallocations and aggregate industry productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: His framework elegantly aggregates micro-level firm heterogeneity into a tractable, balanced macroeconomic model of trade. I value how it reconciles aggregate productivity growth with continuous firm entry and exit, providing a robust benchmark. A reservation is whether it relies on overly stylized functional forms for productivity distributions.

nominations.contribution: for their theoretical contributions to the political economy of trade policy
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They formalized the political economy of trade by embedding lobbying and special interests into a general-equilibrium framework. Their model remains mathematically tractable while accurately reflecting complex empirical regularities in tariff structures. One reservation is its assumption of complete information and perfect substitutability of political contributions.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of global value chains and the organization of international trade
key_works: Antràs, 2003: Firms, contracts, and trade structure, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: He integrated the theory of the firm with international trade, explicitly modeling how global value chains aggregate up to determine trade flows. This provides a structural, micro-founded understanding of international production networks. A limitation is the heavy reliance on specific contracting frictions that can be difficult to quantify.

nominations.contribution: for their development of the new open economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: They established the new open economy macroeconomics, bringing rigorous micro-foundations and dynamic general equilibrium to international finance. Their models successfully replaced ad hoc aggregate formulations with cleanly aggregated structural frameworks. A reservation is that the empirical fit for short-run exchange rate movements remains challenging.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of local labor market adjustments to international trade shocks
key_works: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson, 2013: The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Their work masterfully links international forces to stark spatial divergence and regional inequality. By examining spatially disaggregated local labor markets, they rigorously identify the structural consequences of globalization, proving that broad shocks have profoundly localized impacts.

nominations.contribution: for the development of quantitative, gravity-based models of international trade and spatial technology diffusion
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: They transformed trade and economic geography by providing a tractable framework that maps theoretical spatial interactions onto real-world, geographically disaggregated data. This methodological bridge is crucial for quantifying long-run spatial convergence and technology spillovers.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm-level heterogeneity and its role in international trade and structural reallocation
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: The focus on how trade forces structural change through the selection of productive firms provides a powerful micro-foundation for aggregate development. It explains the underlying reallocation mechanisms that drive long-run national and regional growth.

nominations.contribution: for the integration of endogenous innovation and technological diffusion into the theory of international trade
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1991: Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: They brilliantly connected long-run growth with global economic integration, offering a theoretical framework that endogenizes the very technological transformations central to historical economic history. Their insights hold up across varying periods of global market integration.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of spatial economic geography, trade costs, and the historical fragmentation of global value chains
key_works: Baldwin, 2016: The Great Convergence, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: His long-run perspective on how declining transport and communication costs reshape the geography of production perfectly captures the historical dynamics of market integration. It provides a vital regional and global spatial lens to understand historical divergence and modern convergence.

nominations.contribution: for their incorporation of firm heterogeneity into international trade theory
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: They fundamentally reoriented international economics to focus on individual firms rather than industries. By showing how heterogeneous productivity limits export participation, they connected trade integration directly to firm-level reallocations and aggregate productivity.

nominations.contribution: for her empirical and theoretical analysis of currency invoicing, exchange rate pass-through, and international pricing
key_works: Gopinath, Itskhoki, and Rigobon, 2010: Currency Choice and Exchange Rate Pass-Through, American Economic Review
Gopinath, 2015: The International Price System, Jackson Hole Symposium
nominations.rationale: Her combination of detailed micro data and elegant theory on invoicing currencies transformed the understanding of pricing-to-market. It perfectly exemplifies how firm-level contracting choices under imperfect competition dictate macro-level exchange-rate transmission.

nominations.contribution: for their development of the New Open Economy Macroeconomics and the analysis of international financial policies
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: By embedding sticky prices, monopoly power, and precise intertemporal choice into open-economy models, they built the modern workhorse framework for international macroeconomics, bridging macro phenomena with micro behavior.

nominations.contribution: for his integration of contract theory into international trade and the analysis of global value chains
key_works: Antràs, 2003: Firms, Contracts, and Trade Structure, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: He successfully integrated incomplete contracting and property rights theories with international trade. This provided a much-needed mechanism design perspective on how multinational firms organize their global value chains.

nominations.contribution: for their analysis of endogenous trade policy and the political economy of protection
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They derived robust empirical implications for trade protection from foundational microeconomic models of lobbying. Their work remains the cornerstone for understanding how interest groups distort trade policy.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of global trade shocks and their impact on local labor markets
key_works: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson, 2013: The China Syndrome, AER
nominations.rationale: This work sets the gold standard for design-based empirical strategies using granular data to identify the effects of global shocks. By mapping these shocks to local inequality and institutional outcomes, they transformed our understanding of trade's distributional consequences.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of firm heterogeneity and intra-industry trade
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: By grounding aggregate trade theory in granular, firm-level heterogeneity, he shifted the field toward the rigorous empirical analysis of micro-level selection and survival. She would highly value this shift toward using administrative micro-data to understand macro-level trade patterns.

nominations.contribution: for their analysis of the political economy of trade policy
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, AER
nominations.rationale: She would appreciate their political economy approach, which treats trade policy not as an abstract choice but as the outcome of institutional constraints, incentives, and lobbying. This aligns closely with her view of policy as an endogenous product of institutional rules.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of global value chains and the contractual boundaries of the multinational firm
key_works: Antras, 2003: Firms, Contracts, and Trade Structure, QJE
nominations.rationale: His integration of contract theory with global value chains highlights how institutional frictions and incomplete information shape international trade patterns. This focus on the micro-institutions of the firm provides a credible foundation for complex trade networks.

nominations.contribution: for her empirical analysis of international pricing and the dominant currency paradigm
key_works: Gopinath et al., 2020: Dominant Currency Paradigm, AER
nominations.rationale: Her creative use of massive, novel datasets on international pricing exposes the micro-level institutional mechanisms that drive exchange rate pass-through. This empirical grounding of macro-level pricing behavior perfectly fits the demand for rigorous, data-driven analysis.

nominations.contribution: for the political economy of trade policy and the analysis of special interest politics
key_works: Grossman & Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Their framework brilliantly formalizes how political participation structures and lobbying generate deviations from impartial administration. This work exemplifies conceptual clarity in linking political accountability to economic outcomes, though empirical tests can struggle with the unobservability of political contributions.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of the local labor market and political consequences of international trade
key_works: Autor, Dorn, & Hanson, 2013: The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: Their rigorous empirical mapping of the 'China Shock' compellingly demonstrates how international economic integration drives domestic political polarization and alters regime dynamics. The reliance on highly granular, high-quality data is exemplary, even if the long-run historical persistence of these effects remains an open question.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm heterogeneity and its implications for international trade dynamics
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: By shifting focus to the micro-level administrative and productivity differences between firms, this work provides a robust framework for understanding how economic shocks propagate. The transparent operationalization of firm entry and exit is highly valuable, though it assumes institutional neutrality across borders.

nominations.contribution: for the foundations of open-economy macroeconomics and the historical analysis of capital mobility
key_works: Obstfeld & Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Their work establishes a crucial baseline for how state capacity interacts with global financial markets over long historical horizons. However, the assumption of seamless market functioning sometimes abstracts away from the distinct political regimes that govern these markets.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of global value chains and the spatial agglomeration of economic activity
key_works: Baldwin, 2016: The Great Convergence: Information Technology and the New Globalization, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: His conceptualization of the unbundling of globalization provides a clear theoretical lens for how modern bureaucratic and production systems span borders. The interdisciplinary relevance is high, though it relies more on broad stylized facts than detailed historical institutional analysis.

nominations.contribution: for their quantitative general equilibrium models of international trade and technology diffusion
key_works: Eaton and Kortum, 2002: Technology, Geography, and Trade, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: They transformed trade theory by providing a strictly micro-founded, quantitative general-equilibrium framework that makes the analysis of global trade flows computationally tractable. Their method allows for disciplined counterfactual policy experiments across multiple asymmetric regions, a hallmark of excellent macro-trade research. The probabilistic formulation of technology is an ingenious methodological breakthrough.

nominations.contribution: for the incorporation of firm heterogeneity into the theory of international trade
key_works: Melitz, 2003: The Impact of Trade on Intra-Industry Reallocations and Aggregate Industry Productivity, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: He integrated micro-level heterogeneity into a tractable industry equilibrium, permanently altering how we evaluate the macroeconomic productivity gains from trade. The work elegantly links firm-level selection mechanisms to aggregate outcomes. While the basic framework relies on some specific distributional assumptions for analytical tractability, it serves as an indispensable workhorse model.

nominations.contribution: for their analysis of the political economy of trade policy and trade-induced growth
key_works: Grossman and Helpman, 1994: Protection for Sale, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They formalized the political economy of trade into coherent, optimizing general-equilibrium frameworks that can be tested structurally. Their work clarifies how vested interests distort macroeconomic policy away from optimal allocations. The tight combination of dynamic incentives and general-equilibrium constraints is masterful.

nominations.contribution: for their foundational work on the microfoundations of open-economy macroeconomics
key_works: Obstfeld and Rogoff, 1995: Exchange Rate Dynamics Redux, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: They brought rigorous dynamic intertemporal optimization and nominal rigidities into open-economy macroeconomics. This framework enables disciplined welfare analysis of exchange rate policies and international shock transmission. Their approach elevated international macro to the methodological standards of modern closed-economy macro.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the theory of global value chains and the organization of international trade
key_works: Antràs, 2003: Firms, Contracts, and Trade Structure, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: He successfully embedded incomplete contracting and firm boundaries into general-equilibrium trade models. This clarifies how micro-level organizational incentives determine global value chains and macroeconomic trade flows. The work elegantly bridges structural industrial organization and international macroeconomics.
